key_insight: MMEmb-R1 integrates generative chain-of-thought reasoning into multimodal embedding learning while preventing shortcut behavior by making reasoning use pair-aware and adaptively controlled, so reasoning helps only when it improves pairwise alignment.
problem_solved: Directly injecting reasoning into embedding training causes structural misalignment with pairwise contrastive objectives and can hurt performance because reasoning is not uniformly helpful across all sample pairs.
method: Pair-Aware Selection: selectively incorporate chain-of-thought reasoning for sample pairs where reasoning improves discriminative signals, avoiding noisy or irrelevant rationale for others.
Adaptive Control: learn a gating/weighting mechanism that modulates the influence of generated reasoning on the embedding objective on a per-pair basis.
Contrastive embedding training augmented with reasoning-enhanced representations to retain alignment with pairwise supervision while leveraging reasoning when beneficial.
impact: Enables practitioners to leverage large multimodal LLM reasoning capabilities without degrading contrastive embedding quality—improving robustness and retrieval/alignment performance in multimodal tasks where reasoning matters.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image+text → optional chain-of-thought generator → pair-aware selector → adaptive gate → multimodal embedding & contrastive loss
Before vs After bar chart: embedding alignment/ retrieval metrics with naive reasoning vs pair-aware adaptive approach
Decision heatmap: when the pair-aware selector and adaptive controller choose to use reasoning across pair types
Schematic icon set: contrastive pairs, reasoning bubble (CoT), gate/slider to represent adaptive control
paper_title: MMEmb-R1: Reasoning-Enhanced Multimodal Embedding with Pair-Aware Selection and Adaptive Control
paper_authors: Yuchi Wang, Haiyang Yu, Weikang Bian, Jiefeng Long, Xiao Liang
